subject: Liability & unwind: allocation of prepaid fees and wind-down assistance
messages:
From: Sara Brown <sara.brown@acme.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Initial redline: LoL + termination mechanics

Marcus — attaching Acme's redline for the MSA + order form. Two specific items Legal is flagging:

1) Limitation of Liability: Acme is asking for a full exclusion of indirect/consequential damages and a mutual cap equal to 24 months of fees. They also want to carve out a IP infringement exception and an SLA-based liquidated damages remedy uncapped.

2) Termination & refunds: for prepaid fees they propose a pro-rata refund for unused months plus a separate recovery right for wind-down assistance (up to 60 days) with defined hourly rates. They want those assistance fees to be outside the LoL cap.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept carve-outs for assistance fees outside the cap, and whether we have appetite for an SLA remedy uncapped? Acme says flexibility here is a deal breaker; we have an internal 12/17 exec review.

Attachments: ACME-Redline_MSA_v3.pdf (redline)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Sara
Corporate Counsel | Acme Corporation
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sara Brown <sara.brown@acme.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redline: LoL + termination mechanics

Sara — thanks for the redline and the clear callouts. High level: we need to preserve predictable unit economics and avoid open-ended operational liability. A few reactions from the product/ops side (copying Rishi for legal detail):

- Consequential/indirect damages: we are comfortable with a mutual exclusion for indirect damages (standard).

- Cap level: 24 months is higher than we typically accept. Our standard is the greater of (i) 12 months of fees and (ii) total fees paid in prior 12 months. That aligns with our risk profile and also captures larger enterprise prepaids. Would Acme consider that compromise?

- SLA liquidated damages: we cannot accept an uncapped SLA remedy tied to availability; that undermines our serving economics. We can offer a capped SLA credit formula (e.g., percentage credit of monthly fees, aggregate cap tied to the LoL).

- Wind-down assistance & prepaid refunds: operationally we can provide a 30- to 90-day transition package. Proposal: prorated refund for unused prepaid term OR apply remaining prepaid as credits during a 30-day wind-down assistance window (customer's choice). If customer requests additional hands-on professional services beyond standard transition (e.g., dedicated engineering support > 40 hours/week), we can bill those at published SOW rates.

Crucially: we prefer that professional services / wind-down assistance be treated as recoverable fees (i.e., not excluded from cap) but billed separately so they don’t create an open-ended liability. If they insist these be outside the cap, legal will push back. Rishi — can you draft suggested language that (a) caps aggregate liability and (b) clarifies that termination refunds (pro-rata) are not intended to be a separate uncapped remedy?

If we can align on these points, I’ll take to Acme's exec review next week.

— Marcus
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Brown <sara.brown@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 14:53:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redline: LoL + termination mechanics

Sara / Tom — thanks for the redline. A few legal points and proposed edits below; I have attached a short markup with inline suggestions (redline-notes-20261214.docx).

1) Cap mechanics: proposed language: "each party's aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) twelve (12) months of fees paid under the Order Form applicable to the claim and (b) the total fees paid by Customer to Supplier in the twelve (12) months prior to the event giving rise to the claim." This protects Redwood for new customers and for large prepaids.

2) Carve-outs: standard carve-outs (fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, IP infringement) remain, but we are not comfortable leaving wind-down assistance and standard prepayment refunds as "outside the cap" by default. Practical approach is: termination refunds (pro-rata) are remedies for prepaid balance and should not expand into consequential damages. Separate professional services requested in connection with wind-down can be invoiced and paid; those invoices would be subject to the cap for liability claims but not as a separate uncapped remedy.

3) SLA remedy: propose a narrowly-tailored credit schedule (e.g., for availability below X% in a billing month, credit Y% of monthly fee; aggregate SLA credits limited to Z% of monthly fee and Z months cap). Do not let an SLA credit serve as a basis for unlimited damages or injunctive relief.

4) Drafting mechanics: recommend explicit definition of "Prepaid Fees", "Wind-down Assistance" and a "Transition Services Statement of Work" reference. Also add a 30-day notice window for termination without cause where refunds are prorated to the effective termination date.

Next steps: I can produce a clean markup reflecting the cap language above and an optional paragraph allowing Acme to purchase an extended wind-down bundle for additional fees (with estimated cap impact disclosed). Marcus / Stephanie — if you want I’ll prepare the alternate paragraph and a short client-facing explanation.

Best,
Rishi
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Brown <sara.brown@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial redline: LoL + termination mechanics

Sara — appreciate the quick turn. We want to close this in time for both teams' procurement windows. To move forward, propose the following two paths so Acme can pick:

Option A (standard):
- LoL: mutual exclusion of indirect damages; aggregate cap = greater of (i) 12 months fees, or (ii) fees paid in prior 12 months.
- Termination: pro-rata refund on prepaid unused months; Redwood to provide up to 30 days of transition assistance (standard, no charge) — anything beyond that billed per SOW.
- SLA: capped credits per month; credits do not constitute damages and are the exclusive monetary remedy for uptime claims.

Option B (expanded assistance package):
- LoL: same cap as Option A but Acme may purchase an "Extended Transition Bundle" (30–90 days) prepaid at execution. Prepaid transition fees are treated as fees for purposes of the cap calculation (i.e., included in the fee pool); Redwood will not concede an uncapped right tied solely to assistance fees.
- Termination: as above, with the added option to apply remaining prepaid transition credits to additional professional services.

If Acme can agree to either Option A or Option B we can provide a short redline that implements that approach and route it to your procurement team. If Acme insists on uncapped SLA remedies or placing wind-down assistance outside the cap, we will need explicit executive sign-off (unlikely).

Can you confirm which option Acme prefers by EOD Wednesday 12/17 so we can meet the exec window? If helpful we can do a 20-min call tomorrow morning.

Thanks — Stephanie
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
